implementation_notes: pact-go v2 is the Go realization: consumer.NewV2Pact(MockHTTPProviderConfig{Consumer, Provider}) creates the mock provider, AddInteraction().Given().UponReceiving().WithRequest("GET", S("/user/10")).WillRespondWith(200).WithBodyMatch(&User{}) declares an interaction, and ExecuteTest(t, func(config MockServerConfig) error {...}) starts the mock server, runs the client and fails the test on any unmatched or missing request. Provider verification is HTTPVerifier{}.VerifyProvider(t, VerifyRequest{ProviderBaseURL, PactFiles}); the library is a cgo wrapper over the shared Rust core, so CGO_ENABLED=1 and the pact-go-installed native library are prerequisites.
code_sketch:
mockProvider, _ := consumer.NewV2Pact(consumer.MockHTTPProviderConfig{
    Consumer: "UserAPIConsumer", Provider: "UserAPI"})

mockProvider.AddInteraction().Given("A user with ID 10 exists").
    UponReceiving("A request for User 10").
    WithRequest("GET", consumer.S("/user/10")).
    WillRespondWith(200).WithBodyMatch(&User{})

err = mockProvider.ExecuteTest(t, func(cfg consumer.MockServerConfig) error {
    user, err := newClient(cfg.Host, cfg.Port).GetUser("10")     // code under test
    assert.Equal(t, 10, user.ID)
    return err
})
pitfalls: cgo is mandatory: CGO_ENABLED=0 or a cross-compiled build without the matching native library fails, and musl provider verification is a documented crash source.
Assertions happen when the mock provider is torn down at the end of ExecuteTest, so a missing interaction surfaces as a test-cleanup failure rather than at the call site.
Contracts are files: the consumer pipeline must publish the freshly generated contract before the provider pipeline runs, or the provider verifies yesterday's expectations.
